signals.title: TOP PRIORITY: search finds the right sub-chunk but there is no way to read just that section — read_note dumps the whole note, forcing grep on raw caches OUTSIDE the MCP.
signals.repro: In a live session ask the brain a question whose answer lives deep in a large note (e.g. ORBIS BOS release plan, ~byte 90k of orbis-bos, 351 KB). search_semantic correctly returns the note at a deep section_idx (e.g. 40002), but the result carries only a 240-char snippet + heading, not the sub-chunk body. read_note returns the entire note as a single-line body, so the agent falls back to Bash grep/Python over .claude/ tool-result cache files to extract the section.
signals.evidence: Live post-ship test (retrieval-recall-correctness): answer was correct (18 P0 Demo / 24 P1 Piloto / 12 SCOR epics) but only after read_note(351 KB) + manual grep/Python on cached tool-results — the read half happened outside the brain-mcp entirely. Sprint fixed findability (T1/T2) but exposed the readability gap.

signals.title: search_semantic over-fetch factor is an inline magic number (k * 4), breaking the module's 'named tunables' convention.
signals.repro: Read brain_mcp/vectors.py search_semantic: `fetch = k * 4` is a literal, while every other knob (_CONNECTIVE_FACTOR, _RRF_K, _SUB_IDX_SCALE, _SPLIT_OVERLAP, _MAX_SUB_CHUNKS) is a named module constant.
signals.evidence: refactorer review round 1: 'The module names every other tuning knob but the over-fetch factor is an inline literal.'

signals.title: Unreachable defensive fallback branch in _split_oversized (dead code that reads as live logic).
signals.repro: In _split_oversized, the final `else: _sliding_window(part, ...)` branch cannot trigger because every producer (_split_on_pattern, _pack_paragraphs) already guarantees output <= limit.
signals.evidence: refactorer review round 1: branch unreachable given current callers; suggest removing or reframing as an assertion.

signals.title: _neighbor_key closure is redefined every loop iteration in search_graph though it closes over nothing loop-variant.
signals.repro: In search_graph, `_neighbor_key` is defined inside `for seed in seeds:` but only reads loop-invariant out_edges/in_edges; hoist above the loop or make it module-level.
signals.evidence: refactorer review round 1: reads as if the sort key depends on the current seed, which it does not.

signals.title: The `num_parts >= _SUB_IDX_SCALE` (>=1000) guard in _section_indices is dead code on the production path.
signals.repro: _emit_chunks truncates body_parts to _MAX_SUB_CHUNKS (512) before calling _section_indices, and 512 < 1000, so the >=1000 raise is only reachable via direct/test calls, never through chunk_note.
signals.evidence: security-auditor review round 2 (suggestion): reachable only in test_section_indices_raises_too_many_parts; add a comment noting it's not load-bearing in production.

signals.title: The `if len(seed_list) > k` branch in search_graph is currently unreachable (search_hybrid already returns <= k seeds).
signals.repro: search_graph builds `results` 1:1 from `seeds = search_hybrid(query, k=k, ...)`, which internally returns sorted(...)[:k]; so len(seed_list) can never exceed k. The truncation branch is untested/unexercised, but is the only guard if search_hybrid's contract ever changes to over-return.
signals.evidence: code-reviewer extra-round verify (suggestion): harmless today, unexercised by any test.
